title: MATH GAOKAO - 278
description: Authentic-style mathematics problems inspired by China’s Gaokao — build deeper understanding, sharper thinking, and real exam readiness.

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Linear Function at a Point
questions.learningObjective: Determine a parameter so that a piecewise linear function is continuous at the joining point.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
x+1, & x<1,\\
ax, & x\ge 1.
\end{cases}
\]
Find the value of \(a\) for which \(f\) is continuous at \(x=1\).
questions.explanation:
Compute the left-hand limit at \(x=1\):
\[
\lim_{x\to 1^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 1^-}(x+1)=2.
\]
The value from the right-hand piece is \(f(1)=a\). For continuity at \(x=1\), we need \(a=2\).
questions.hint: Compare the left-hand limit at \(x=1\) with the value of the right-hand piece at \(x=1\).

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Quadratic-Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Find a parameter so that a piecewise function with a quadratic and a linear piece is continuous at the joining point.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
x^2, & x<2,\\
mx+1, & x\ge 2.
\end{cases}
\]
Find the value of \(m\) for which \(f\) is continuous at \(x=2\).
questions.explanation:
The left-hand limit at \(x=2\) is
\[
\lim_{x\to 2^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 2^-}x^2=4.
\]
The right-hand value is \(f(2)=2m+1\). For continuity, we need
\[
2m+1=4.
\]
Thus \(2m=3\), so \(m=\frac{3}{2}\).
questions.hint: Set the left-hand limit equal to the value of the right-hand piece at \(x=2\), then solve for \(m\).

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Linear-Quadratic Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine a parameter so that a piecewise function is continuous at a point.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
2x+a, & x<3,\\
x^2-1, & x\ge 3.
\end{cases}
\]
Find the value of \(a\) for which \(f\) is continuous at \(x=3\).
questions.explanation:
The left-hand limit at \(x=3\) is
\[
\lim_{x\to 3^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 3^-}(2x+a)=6+a.
\]
The right-hand value is
\[
f(3)=3^2-1=8.
\]
For continuity, we need \(6+a=8\), so \(a=2\).
questions.hint: Evaluate both pieces at \(x=3\) and set the results equal.

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Quadratic-Linear Function with a Parameter
questions.learningObjective: Find a parameter that makes a piecewise function continuous at its joining point.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
x^2+a, & x<2,\\
3x-1, & x\ge 2.
\end{cases}
\]
Find the value of \(a\) for which \(f\) is continuous at \(x=2\).
questions.explanation:
The left-hand limit at \(x=2\) is
\[
\lim_{x\to 2^-}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 2^-}(x^2+a)=4+a.
\]
The right-hand value is
\[
f(2)=3(2)-1=5.
\]
For continuity, we need \(4+a=5\), so \(a=1\).
questions.hint: Compare the limiting value from the left with the value from the right at \(x=2\).

questions.concept: Removing a Removable Discontinuity of a Trigonometric Function
questions.learningObjective: Find the value at the origin that makes a trigonometric piecewise function continuous.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{\sin x}{x}, & x\neq 0,\\
k, & x=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Find \(k\) so that \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
questions.explanation:
The standard trigonometric limit gives
\[
\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sin x}{x}=1.
\]
For continuity at \(x=0\), we need
\[
k=\lim_{x\to 0}f(x)=1.
\]
Thus \(k=1\).
questions.hint: Recall the standard limit of \(\frac{\sin x}{x}\) as \(x\to 0\).

questions.concept: Removing a Removable Discontinuity Involving \(1-\cos x\)
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value at the origin that makes a trigonometric piecewise function continuous.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{1-\cos x}{x^2}, & x\neq 0,\\
k, & x=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Find \(k\) so that \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
questions.explanation:
The standard limit is
\[
\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{1-\cos x}{x^2}=\frac{1}{2}.
\]
For continuity at \(x=0\), we need
\[
k=\lim_{x\to 0}f(x)=\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Therefore \(k=\frac{1}{2}\).
questions.hint: Recall the standard limit involving \(1-\cos x\) and \(x^2\) as \(x\to 0\).

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Function Involving the Tangent Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine a parameter so that a piecewise function with a tangent quotient is continuous at the origin.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{\tan(ax)}{x}, & x\neq 0,\\
3, & x=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Find the value of \(a\) for which \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
questions.explanation:
Using the standard limit \(\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{\tan t}{t}=1\), with \(t=ax\), we get
\[
\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\tan(ax)}{x}
=
a\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\tan(ax)}{ax}
=
a.
\]
For continuity at \(x=0\), we need
\[
a=f(0)=3.
\]
Thus \(a=3\).
questions.hint: Use the standard limit \(\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{\tan t}{t}=1\) and compare it with \(f(0)\).

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Function Involving an Exponential Quotient
questions.learningObjective: Find a parameter so that a piecewise function with an exponential quotient is continuous at the origin.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{e^{ax}-1}{x}, & x\neq 0,\\
2, & x=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Find the value of \(a\) for which \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
questions.explanation:
Using the standard limit \(\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{e^t-1}{t}=1\), with \(t=ax\), we obtain
\[
\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^{ax}-1}{x}
=
a\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{e^{ax}-1}{ax}
=
a.
\]
For continuity at \(x=0\), we need
\[
a=f(0)=2.
\]
Therefore \(a=2\).
questions.hint: Use the standard limit \(\lim_{t\to 0}\frac{e^t-1}{t}=1\) and compare it with \(f(0)\).

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Function Involving a Square Root
questions.learningObjective: Determine the value at the origin that makes a square-root piecewise function continuous.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{\sqrt{x+1}-1}{x}, & x\neq 0,\\
k, & x=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Find \(k\) so that \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
questions.hint: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate \(\sqrt{x+1}+1\), then evaluate the limit.

questions.concept: Continuity of a Piecewise Function Involving an Exponential Power
questions.learningObjective: Find a parameter so that a piecewise function involving \((1+ax)^{1/x}\) is continuous at the origin.
questions.question:
Let
\[
f(x)=
\begin{cases}
(1+ax)^{1/x}, & x\neq 0,\\
e^2, & x=0.
\end{cases}
\]
Find the positive value of \(a\) for which \(f\) is continuous at \(x=0\).
questions.explanation:
Take the natural logarithm of the expression for \(x\neq 0\):
\[
\ln(1+ax)^{1/x}=\frac{\ln(1+ax)}{x}.
\]
Using \(\ln(1+u)\approx u\) for small \(u\), or the standard limit,
\[
\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\ln(1+ax)}{x}=a.
\]
Thus,
\[
\lim_{x\to 0}(1+ax)^{1/x}=e^a.
\]
For continuity at \(x=0\), we need
\[
e^a=e^2,
\]
so \(a=2\). Since \(a>0\), the value is \(a=2\).
questions.hint: Take the natural logarithm and use the standard limit \(\lim_{u\to 0}\frac{\ln(1+u)}{u}=1\).
